newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS-FX vol curves steepen as spot consolidates.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-FX vol curves steepen as spot consolidates.

text.p: Implied volatility curves for dollar-pair options steepened as consolidative spot rates pressured the front end, traders said.

The back months were more resilient due to expectations the dollar would eventually surge toward the upside strike prices, in which dealers tended to be short after big end-user purchases recently in those maturities, they added.
"These curve changes have much more to do with demand," said MaryBeth Slack, FX options analyst at MCM OptionWatch. "They do much less with spot movement because we're not getting any spot movement."
She said spot dollar/yen did not look eager to test the 119-yen level for now, perhaps as the market awaited Friday's July U.S. employment report.

"People are taking a little bit of a breather ahead of non-farm payrolls," she said, adding that the numbers were unlikely to surprise the market too much. Economists polled by Reuters have forecast, on average, a 193,000 rise in July non-farm payrolls against June's 217,000 gain.
One-month dollar/yen volatility stood at 11.0/11.3 percent at U.S. midsession, down nearly half a point from Wednesday's levels. One-year was a hair easier at 11.8/12.0 percent.
Dollar/mark volatilities bounced off early lows as spot rebounded toward 1.84 marks from lows around 1.83, but the front end was struggling under the weight of time decay and the curve steepened.
One-month dollar/mark was quoted at 9.8/10.1 percent, up 0.1 point or so from early lows but off Wednesday's levels at 10.2/10.4. One-year was steady at 10.4/10.6 percent.
"One-year's been really sticky," said a U.S. bank dealer in Chicago. "It really hasn't moved in the last few days."
Some buying was seen in short-dated low-delta mark puts, although the front end was generally soft, he added.
"With everything so rangey, you have to expect implieds to come off," Slack noted.
"I think it might be worthwhile looking at cable and sterling/mark," she added, pointing out that the Bank of England's August 6-7 monetary policy committee meeting could generate volatility.
"I think those vols are going to stay fairly firm -- the front end of cable and sterling/mark -- until that time, even though spot's not doing much," she said.
She said one-week cable, at around 9.0 percent, had fallen below the historical volatility and could be offering value.
One-month cable was assessed at 8.8/9.1 percent, off more than half a point on the day. Slack said that level was roughly where corresponding historical volatility stood.

The sterling bounced above $1.64 from Wednesday's low near $1.62 after a sharp selloff earlier in the week. That decline was seen as a correction to the strong rally in the preceeding months based on expectation of higher British interest rates.
Traders said appointments of two new deputy governors at the British central bank earlier in the day seemed to be strenghtening the bank's anti-inflation stance.
